{{Short description|American physicist (1922–1991)}}
'''Stanley Howard Autler''' (March 28, 1922 &ndash; October 16, 1991)<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zldAAQAAIAAJ&q=%22Autler,+Stanley%22+AND+%221922%22 |title = Who's who in Government|year = 1972}}</ref> was an American physicist.

After receiving bachelor's and master's degrees from the [[City College of New York]], he was award his Ph.D. from [[Columbia University]].<ref name=itas5_2_121/> Thereafter he joined the staff of Lincoln Laboratory at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he performed research on low temperature physics, [[solid state physics]] and high [[magnetic field]] [[superconductivity]].<ref name=9aaies/> In 1955, he and [[Charles Hard Townes|Charles H. Townes]] demonstrated a new dynamic [[Stark effect]], later known as the [[Autler–Townes effect]]. This occurs when "a [[microwave]] [[Atomic electron transition|transition]] can be split into two components when one of the two levels involved in the transition is coupled to a third one by a strong [[Radio frequency|RF]] field" (Picque and Pinard 1976).<ref name=jpb9_5_L77/>

Autler was a pioneer in the use of small superconducting solenoids with [[niobium]] wire, producing a 2.5&nbsp;[[Tesla (unit)|T]] field at a temperature of 4.2&nbsp;[[Kelvin|K]], then achieving 9.8&nbsp;T at a temperature of 1.5&nbsp;K.<ref name=itas5_2_121/> He may have been the first person to create an application for superconductivity when he used this magnetic field for a solid state [[maser]].<ref name=lee2001/> This led to widespread interest in the practical uses of superconducting magnets. In 1960, he filed for a patent for a superconducting magnet, which was awarded in 1965.<ref name=sb8_1/> In 1963, he was named head of the Low Temperature Physics section at the [[Westinghouse Electric (1886)|Westinghouse]] Research Laboratories.<ref name=science142_3598/>

He was married to his wife Kaja and the couple had a daughter Lilian who graduated from [[Yale University]].<ref name=itas5_2_121/>
